description: We are the Robotic Society, consisting of a group of UC Merced students with a wide range of skills in computer science, storytelling, electrical engineering, and mechanical engineering.
summary: The Robotics Society Team develops a video game where 1-4 players devise and build a spacecraft that can traverse space and dodge obstacles to rescue the astronauts aboard the International Space Station (ISS). The game has up to 7 levels. Each level introduces new constraints and unlocks more spacecraft configuration options. The game meets various aspects of the original challenge, including mission design, spacecraft & payload, orbit & launch, resource management, and educational value. In the mission design aspect, players must make choices that reflect real decisions in space mission design. To meet the spacecraft/payload and resource management aspects of the challenge, players must manage resources and choose a best-fit combination of spacecraft components to meet various constraints and requirements. The game bridges the gap between aspiring engineers and curious minds who want to experiment and learn the many factors involved in space mission design.
details:
Starliner - Rescue Mission is a pixel video game where 1-4 players customize a rescue craft and plot a trajectory to safely reach the International Space Station (ISS), while managing fuel and budget. There are a total of 7 levels that introduce players to the design aspect of the spacecraft, with each subsequent level introducing a new challenge, objective, and additional information.

At the beginning of the level, the entire course (from Kennedy Space Center Launch Complex to ISS) will be shown to player(s), including component data and distance. Player(s) are instructed to build the spacecraft and leverage parts against each other, balancing power, fuel efficiency, heat resistance, and weight while considering the change in direction and thrusters. The decisions the player(s) make will impact the mission's success. The mission is successful when the spacecraft boards the ISS and returns to Earth (Gulf of Mexico). Poor decisions can cause the spacecraft to miss the ISS, failing the mission. Once the level is completed, player(s) can move on to the next level. The game also has a special “Sandbox” mode that allows player(s) to experiment with all available spacecraft designs and data with an unlimited budget. 

The game provides an accessible means of building engineering and executive decision-making skills in a consequence-free environment, with each level proving to be challenging. Our team hopes to bridge all aspects of spacecraft design, resource management, route planning, and re-entry considerations in our game. 

Our team uses many software tools to bring this game to life (as intended): Python, with Pygame for coding; Canva for the project demo; Procreate for designing the pixel art; SoundATON for the soundtrack; Google Docs to store information; and GitHub to store and track the source code. We also used AI in our project development; more information will be provided in the “Use of Super Intelligence (SI)” section.

SI was utilized for code and visual assets, excluding pixel art. Many code-defined values, including gravity and fuel consumption, were left as-is. SI was not used for music or sound effects. SI agents used include ChatGPT and Perplexity.
